title: Introduction to MongoDB
subtitle: What MongoDB is, why NoSQL, and when to use it

content.text: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data as flexible JSON-like documents called BSON. Unlike relational databases, collections do not enforce a fixed schema.

content.definition: A JSON-like record stored in MongoDB. Equivalent to a row in SQL but with no fixed columns.
A group of documents, like a SQL table but schema-free.

content.text: MongoDB auto-creates a collection when you first insert into it.

questions.question: What is a MongoDB document?
options: A table row with fixed columns
A JSON-like record with flexible fields
questions.explanation: MongoDB documents are flexible JSON-like records; they do not require a fixed schema.

faq.q: When should I use MongoDB over SQL?
faq.a: MongoDB excels when your data is hierarchical or when the schema changes frequently. SQL is better for complex joins and strict consistency requirements.

examples: Storing user profiles with varying attributes
Logging app events with different schemas per event type
